jobs/ln: Layer norm does two jobs on a token's vector. It re-centers: subtract the mean. And it re-scales: divide by the standard deviation. Then come a learned gain, gamma, and shift, beta.
jobs/rms: RMSNorm keeps only the re-scaling. No mean and no shift: it divides by the root mean square, then multiplies by gamma.
jobs/why: The re-scaling turned out to be the part that matters, and skipping the mean saves work on every token.
rms/x: Take a token's vector: one, minus five, five and seven.
rms/sq: Square every entry: one, twenty five, twenty five, forty nine.
rms/mean: Their mean is a hundred over four: twenty five.
rms/root: Its square root is five. That is the root mean square, the size of a typical entry.
rms/out: Divide by it: zero point two, minus one, one, and one point four. Now the root mean square is exactly one.
rms/gain: Last, each feature is multiplied by its own learned gain gamma, which starts at one. That is d parameters, where layer norm has two d.
shift/scale: Multiply x by three, and its root mean square triples too. The output does not change.
shift/shift: But add three to every entry, and RMSNorm's output moves, because it never subtracts the mean. Layer norm would not notice. That is the whole price of dropping the mean.
